title: Solister elevation and reference-shape catalog
projectionNote: Stored maps use a 2:1 equirectangular grid. The app converts their texel locations to the IAU/NAIF body-fixed frame before vertex displacement.

PDS/USGS MGS MOLA MEGDR
sources.role: Mars global MOLA median topography; 4 px/degree, GMM3 (mgm1025) degree/order 50 areoid datum.

mercury.name: Mercury
mercury.source: MESSENGER Global DEM, USGS Astrogeology, 665.243 m/pixel (64 px/degree)
mercury.citation: USGS Astrogeology Science Center, Mercury MESSENGER USGS DEM Global 665m v2.
mercury.sourceProjection: Equirectangular; planetocentric latitude; positive-east longitude; global.
mercury.sourceVerticalDatum: Heights scaled by 0.5 m per stored signed-int16 DN above a 2,439.4 km reference sphere.
mercury.referenceShape: IAU/NAIF PCK pck00011.tpc ellipsoid (2,440.53 x 2,438.26 km); source-sphere elevations converted to radial offsets from that ellipsoid.

venus.name: Venus
venus.source: Magellan global radar-altimetry topography, USGS Astrogeology, 4,641.0589 m/pixel (~22.8 px/degree).
venus.citation: USGS Astrogeology Science Center, Venus Magellan Topography Global 4641m v02.
venus.sourceProjection: Simple cylindrical/equirectangular; global; signed int16 metres.
venus.sourceVerticalDatum: Source GeoTIFF uses a 6,051.0 km spherical datum; converted by -800 m to the 6,051.8 km IAU mean radius.
venus.referenceShape: IAU/NAIF PCK pck00011.tpc mean spherical radius 6,051.8 km.

moon.name: Moon
moon.source: NASA LRO LOLA CGI Moon Kit LDEM_4, 4 px/degree (~7.58 km/pixel at the equator).
moon.citation: NASA Goddard Scientific Visualization Studio, CGI Moon Kit (LOLA displacement map).
moon.sourceProjection: Simple cylindrical; planetocentric latitude; positive-east longitude; 0–360 E.
moon.sourceVerticalDatum: Unsigned DN encodes radius = 1,727,400 m + 0.5 m*DN; subtracting the 1,737,400 m IAU reference radius gives elevation = (DN - 20,000)*0.5 m.
moon.referenceShape: LOLA/IAU spherical reference radius 1,737.4 km (NAIF PCK pck00011.tpc).

mars.name: Mars
mars.source: MGS MOLA MEGDR global median topography, PDS Geosciences Node MEGT90N000CB, 4 px/degree (0.25 degree).
mars.citation: Smith et al. MOLA; USGS Astrogeology / PDS Geosciences Node MEGDR v1.0, product version 2.0.
mars.sourceProjection: Simple cylindrical; 1,440 x 720; planetocentric; positive-east 0–360 E; cell centres.
mars.sourceVerticalDatum: Median topography above the GMM3 (mgm1025) degree/order 50 areoid; signed big-endian int16 metres. Cells without observations are interpolated in the supplied MEGDR product.
mars.referenceShape: NAIF PCK pck00011.tpc IAU ellipsoid (3,396.19 x 3,376.20 km). Areoid-to-ellipsoid undulation is not applied; source heights are radial offsets.

earth.name: Earth
earth.source: NOAA ETOPO1 Ice Surface global relief model, 1 arc-minute native grid (21601 x 10801).
earth.citation: Amante, C. & Eakins, B. W. (2009), ETOPO1 1 Arc-Minute Global Relief Model, NOAA Technical Memorandum NESDIS NGDC-24.
earth.sourceProjection: Grid-registered geographic WGS 84, 1 arc-minute; longitude -180 to +180 with a duplicated seam; latitude +90 to -90.
earth.sourceVerticalDatum: Whole-metre signed int16 elevations relative to sea level; Ice Surface version (top of Greenland/Antarctic ice sheets). Geoid-to-ellipsoid separation is not applied.
earth.referenceShape: NAIF PCK pck00011.tpc WGS-84-like Earth ellipsoid (6,378.1366 x 6,356.7519 km); sea-level elevations applied radially to this shape.
